Love Offering
luv AW-fer-ing
noun phrase
A church-finance idiom for a freewill, over-and-above gift — collected for a guest preacher, a missionary, a family in need, or a special cause — given out of affection rather than obligation. The phrase joins the affection of Christian love to the ancient category of the freewill offering.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

⚖️ Biblical Verdict

🟡
Neutral
A sound and commended freewill gift of love (2 Cor. 9:7); fine, with only a mild caution to handle it honestly and openly.

📖 Biblical Definition

A freewill gift of love is squarely biblical; Scripture commends exactly this kind of cheerful, uncompelled generosity. 'Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver' (2 Cor. 9:7). Under the law the freewill offering stood beside the required ones: 'the men, both heart willing... brought a willing offering unto the LORD' (Exod. 35:22). The early church gathered to relieve the saints (Acts 11:29; Rom. 15:26), and Paul taught that 'they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel' (1 Cor. 9:14), commending the Philippians who supplied his need so that fruit might 'abound to your account' (Phil. 4:17). A love offering, rightly meant, is this very thing: a gift purposed in the heart and given gladly, to honor a servant of Christ or to bear a brother's burden. The category is sound and the motive is commended.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A church-finance idiom for a freewill, over-and-above gift given out of affection; basically sound (2 Cor. 9:7), with only a mild caution against using the warm label to obscure ordinary honesty about money.

LOVE OFFERING, noun phrase. A freewill, over-and-above gift collected out of affection — for a guest, a missionary, or one in need.

Joins Christian love to the ancient category of the freewill offering (Exod. 35:29).

Apt sense: cheerful, uncompelled giving — 'not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver' (2 Cor. 9:7).

Cautioned sense: the warm label occasionally used to blur plain accountability — an off-the-books collection where honest, transparent stewardship is owed.

📖 Key Scripture

2 Corinthians 9:7 — "Every man according as he purposeth in his heart, so let him give; not grudgingly, or of necessity: for God loveth a cheerful giver."

Exodus 35:29 — "The children of Israel brought a willing offering unto the LORD, every man and woman, whose heart made them willing to bring for all manner of work, which the LORD had commanded to be made by the hand of Moses."

Philippians 4:18 — "But I have all, and abound: I am full, having received of Epaphroditus the things which were sent from you, an odour of a sweet smell, a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God."

1 Corinthians 9:14 — "Even so hath the Lord ordained that they which preach the gospel should live of the gospel."

2 Corinthians 8:12 — "For if there be first a willing mind, it is accepted according to that a man hath, and not according to that he hath not."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Basically no corruption to name — this is a sound and commended practice; only a mild caution that the warm label must not be used to dodge plain honesty and accountability about money.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition; the practice is good, and the caution is narrow and practical. A love offering is simply the freewill, cheerful giving Scripture praises — 'God loveth a cheerful giver' (2 Cor. 9:7) — whether to honor a visiting preacher, support a missionary, or relieve a family in distress. There is nothing here to recover from the culture; it is one of the gladder corners of church life. The only danger is the danger that attends all money in ministry: that a tender-sounding label can become a cover for loose or self-serving handling of funds.

The watchfulness Scripture commends is over honesty and motive, not over generosity. Paul was scrupulous to handle the saints' gifts 'honestly, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men' (2 Cor. 8:21), and he 'avoid[ed] this, that no man should blame us in this abundance which is administered by us' (2 Cor. 8:20). A 'love offering' that becomes an unaccounted, undeclared, preacher-enriching collection — the kind the prosperity hucksters have made a trade of — is no longer the freewill gift Scripture commends but a snare, for 'the love of money is the root of all evil' (1 Tim. 6:10). The cure is plain stewardship: count it openly, report it honestly, give it as designated.

The recovery is simply to keep the love offering what it is — love. Give cheerfully and purpose it in the heart (2 Cor. 9:7); receive it gratefully as Paul received the Philippians' gift, 'a sacrifice acceptable, wellpleasing to God' (Phil. 4:18); and handle it transparently before God and men. A church that loves its servants will gladly support them, and a church that fears God will do it in the light. So kept, the love offering is no mere idiom but a sweet-smelling sacrifice, and the cheerful giver is one God loves.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

A freewill gift of love, squarely biblical and commended (2 Cor. 9:7; Phil. 4:18); the only caution is plain honesty in handling it — counted openly and given as designated, never a cover for loose stewardship.

expand to see more

English: Christian love joined to the ancient freewill offering (Exod. 35:29) — a glad, over-and-above gift.

Greek: the cheerful giver, hilaron doten (2 Cor. 9:7) — giving purposed in the heart, not grudged or compelled.

The safeguard: 2 Cor. 8:20-21, funds handled 'honestly... in the sight of men' — love offering kept in the light.

Usage

"They received a love offering for the visiting missionary, counted it openly, and sent it on as designated — a sacrifice wellpleasing to God."

"God loveth a cheerful giver; the love offering is gladness purposed in the heart, not a sum grudged or compelled."

"Keep it love and keep it honest: the warm label is no excuse for loose handling, for the love of money is a root of all evil."
